```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(rstan)
library(bayesplot)
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(lubridate)
```

## Preparation

```{r Preparation}
# Helper function to convert H:MM:SS to total minutes
time_to_minutes <- function(time_str) {
  parts <- as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(time_str, ":")))
  if (length(parts) == 3) {
    return(parts[1] * 60 + parts[2] + parts[3] / 60)
  } else {
    return(parts[1] + parts[2] / 60)
  }
}
df_og <- read.csv("data/repeated_ids_with_countries.csv")

mean_age <- mean(df_og$Age)
sd_age <- sd(df_og$Age)

df_time <- df_og %>%
  mutate(
    minutes = sapply(`Official.Time`, time_to_minutes),
    log_time = log(minutes),
    runner_id = as.numeric(as.factor(ID)),
    country_id = as.numeric(as.factor(Country)),
    year_id = as.numeric(as.factor(Year)),
    sex_numeric = ifelse(`M.F` == "M", 1, 0),
    age_std = (Age - mean_age) / sd_age,
    age2_std = age_std^2
  )
df_clean <- df_time %>%
  filter(!is.na(log_time)) # Remove any rows with missing times

# Note: For large datasets (Boston has ~30k runners/year),
# you might want to take a sample for testing:
# df <- df %>% sample_n(2000)
df <- df_clean %>% sample_n(3000)
# 2. Prepare data list for Stan
stan_data <- list(
  N = nrow(df),
  log_time = df$log_time,
  sex = df$sex_numeric,
  age = df$Age,
  age2 = df$age2
)
```



## Including Plots

```{r runModel}
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

model.base <- stan(
  file = "stan_models/baseModel.stan",
  data = stan_data,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 5000,
  control = list(
    adapt_delta = 0.95,
    max_treedepth = 15 # Aumentado de 10 a 15
  )
)
```


```{r results}
target_pars <- c("beta0", "beta_sex", "beta_age", "beta_age2", "sigma", "nu")

p_trace <- mcmc_trace(model.base, pars = target_pars) +
  ggtitle("Trace Plots (Filtered Parameters)")

# 3. Create Distribution (Posterior Density) Plots
p_dens <- mcmc_dens(model.base, pars = target_pars) +
  ggtitle("Posterior Distributions")

print(model_summary)

posterior_samples <- as.array(model.base, pars = target_pars)
df_pooled <- tibble(
  county = county_name,
  model = "pooled",
  intercept = mean(posterior_samples$beta0),
  slope = mean(posterior_samples$beta_age),
  slope_sex = mean(posterior_samples$beta_sex),
  slope_age = mean(posterior_samples$beta_age),
  slope_age2 = mean(posterior_samples$beta_age2)
)
```

```{r}
mean_sex_effect <- mean(posterior_samples$beta_sex)
cat("On average, being female changes log time by:", mean_sex_effect)
```

```{r}
post_samples <- as.data.frame(posterior_samples)

# Generate predictions for a range of ages
age_range <- seq(min(df_clean$Age), max(df_clean$Age), length.out = 100)
pred_df <- map_df(age_range, function(a) {
  mu_samples <- post_samples$beta0 + post_samples$beta_age * a + post_samples$beta_age2 * (a^2)
  tibble(
    Age = a,
    log_time_pred = mean(mu_samples),
    low = quantile(mu_samples, 0.025),
    high = quantile(mu_samples, 0.975)
  )
})

ggplot(pred_df, aes(x = Age, y = log_time_pred)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), alpha = 0.2, fill = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = df_clean, aes(x = Age, y = log_time)) +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior Predictive: Log(Time) vs Age",
    subtitle = "Blue line shows mean relationship for Males",
    y = "log(Time in Minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
